sections.title: Permanent working directories
sections.body: Panel: /opt/remnacust/panel/.env and /opt/remnacust/panel/docker-compose.yml. Node: /opt/remnacust/node/.env and /opt/remnacust/node/docker-compose.yml. Standalone subscription page: /opt/remnacust/subscription-page/.env with docker-compose.yml beside it. Do not create another .env in /opt/remnacust itself. Each service has one working directory without a date suffix. Additional pages can use explicitly selected permanent directories. .env is hidden; use ls -la to list it.

sections.title: Edit and apply changes
sections.body: For the panel, run cd /opt/remnacust/panel, then nano .env or nano docker-compose.yml. Save, validate with docker compose config --quiet, then apply with docker compose up -d --no-build --pull never. For a node or page, enter its directory first. docker compose restart does not reload environment variables; up -d recreates affected containers. Recreation may briefly interrupt connections. Do not arbitrarily replace APP_SECRET, SECRET_KEY or existing database credentials: they are tied to saved data and access.

sections.title: Older date-suffixed installations
sections.body: Start with cat /opt/remnacust/FILES.txt to locate the active deployment and Compose file. Updates move owned legacy panel-<date>-<number> and node-<date>-<number> directories to permanent panel and node paths. Environment-file and bind-mount paths move with them; secrets, Docker volumes and stopped-service state are preserved. Failed verification rolls the move back. To relocate separately, run remnacust normalize-layout --component panel or --component node. Unused old directories go to backups/retired-layout. Paths used by another container and explicitly selected external deployments are not moved blindly; FILES.txt records their actual paths.

sections.title: Other files and data
sections.body: backups/ holds backups and rollback history, logs/ operation logs, registry/ active deployment records, and control/ the local panel-update channel. These are not additional working panel copies. PostgreSQL, cache and backup data may live in Docker volumes. Moving the working directory does not create a new database or replace existing volumes. Root and service FILES.txt maps list the files actually in use. Data and saved secrets remain unchanged after relocation.

sections.title: Main sections
sections.body: Users are accounts and their access settings. Nodes are connection servers. Profiles define Xray configuration, while hosts define the connection addresses shown in subscriptions. Internal squads connect users to permitted inbound connections. For your initial setup, follow “First working connection”.

sections.title: What determines access
sections.body: A connection requires a working node, an active profile inbound, an available host and an internal squad permitting that inbound. User status, subscription expiry, traffic quota and device restrictions also apply. Host and tag limits are separate from the user’s overall quota.

sections.title: Checking changes
sections.body: After saving, check the updated values in the detail view. If a connection still uses the previous settings, check node status and logs, then refresh the subscription in the client.

sections.title: A day without the panel
sections.body: Autonomous policy does not stop merely because the panel is unreachable. A planned day requires an applied policy, persistent volumes, valid credentials and enough local credit for every user, host and tag limit. A user’s total remaining quota is distributed across nodes and is not the credit of each node. Subscription expiry, exhausted credit and quota-period boundaries still deny access. The panel must fund the next period after a reset; the current implementation does not fund it offline. CDN, DNS, proxy and node certificates must remain independent. Recreating a container requires persistent state directories. A core loaded through CUSTOM_CORE_URL also needs its source to be reachable. Blocks or freezes changed during the outage arrive after reconnection. A maintenance readiness check proves current state, not a guaranteed day of traffic.

sections.title: Maintenance logs and long-running service
sections.body: Detailed CLI logs are /opt/remnacust/logs/installer-panel.log, installer-node.log and installer-subscription-page.log. Status checks use a separate log and retain the last update log. The next action for the same component replaces its previous log; a parallel invocation cannot erase an active log. Browser panel updates retain panel-update-<ID>.log, page operations retain page-<page ID>-<job ID>.log, and SSH node maintenance retains node-maintenance.log on that node. Failures show the path. Logs are root-only and never part of public subscriptions. Input and secret tracing are not recorded. APT confirmation is automatic; configuration questions remain interactive over SSH. Configuration caches are bounded by count and size; oversized entries bypass the local cache but remain available from the source. Completion, errors and disconnects release capacity when work settles. Original SQL histories match published Remnawave 3.0.0, 3.4.3 and 3.4.8; unknown or modified history stops migration before application changes.

sections.title: Nodes while the panel is offline
sections.body: A node with a confirmed autonomous policy continues serving saved keys without the panel, including XHTTP through a CDN pointing directly at the node. Access expiry, quotas, speeds and rules remain enforced locally. Exhausted credit or expiry still denies access. New users, renewals and blocks arrive after reconnection. Before stopping applications, the installer checks node autonomy. Unconfirmed readiness produces a warning and the update continues without an extra flag. Panel-dependent nodes may temporarily lose connectivity. Legacy policy without local reserves expires after 90 seconds; simply disabling that deadline is unsafe. Manual docker compose down bypasses the check and also stops a node or proxy in the same project.

sections.title: Update progress and logs
sections.body: Panel updates show eight stages, elapsed time and the last 24 events. Remaining time is estimated only when a previous operation supplies timing data; otherwise remaining stages are shown. Closing the tab does not cancel the update. The service pins a fresh installer release before checking and installing it; a newer verified panel may supersede an outdated notification target. Successful updates keep current, previous and container-used images while removing redundant component images. The panel does not receive the Docker socket.

sections.title: Browser refresh after an update
sections.body: After the build changes, open administrator tabs check the panel version and reload automatically. Data caches, view preferences and table state reset. Authentication, saved templates, history, the SSH vault and pending maintenance intents are preserved. An in-flight mutation is not interrupted. Visible tabs check every 45 seconds and when revisited; an unavailable panel is checked again after recovery. Server settings and user data are not cleared. Tabs from releases without this check need one initial page refresh. The upcoming update persists a local profile/template draft before reloading. If persistence fails, automatic reload is cancelled. Recovery is available in “History → Unsaved draft” and is never applied without your choice. Older open tabs without recovery can still lose text; copy it first.

sections.title: Supported operating systems and PostgreSQL
sections.body:
Installer 1.2.141 accepts Ubuntu 22.04/24.04/26.04 LTS and Debian 12/13, amd64/arm64. Docker uses the official repository for the installed distribution. Interim Ubuntu releases and derivative distributions are not accepted automatically. The amd64 matrix checks real userspace, Bash, Python, OpenSSL and unit workflows; it does not replace kernel boot, systemd, firewall or arm64 tests.

All 195 migrations, quota, expiry and diagnostics scenarios were checked on PostgreSQL 14.24/15.19/16.15/17.11/18.6 as a non-superuser database owner. For new installations, choose a supported major version with current fixes. PostgreSQL 14 support ends on November 12, 2026; PostgreSQL 13 was not tested and is end-of-life. Major upgrades require a separate pg_upgrade or dump/restore. Do not open an old data volume with a new major image; verify the migration on a copy first.

sections.title: Template freshness
sections.body: The cache revision is read from one PostgreSQL metadata row and changes in the same transaction as the template. Rollback does not publish a new revision. Redis cleanup failures cannot leave other API processes serving the old template. Reads do not scan users or template rows; personal HWID, permissions and delivery remain independent.

sections.title: Network storage and cold caches
sections.body:
Network-backed block storage does not by itself make a server incompatible. Read/write latency, available IOPS and durability of acknowledged writes matter. After PostgreSQL or the OS starts, some data is not yet in memory. Later improvement may be cache warming, but does not prove that queries are efficient. Compare cold and warm subscription latency, disk load and database waits. Do not clear a production database cache merely to test it.

Concurrent reads of the same raw template share one query within an API process when the shared cache is available. Personal rendering, HWID and access checks are not shared. Identical geofile builds also share bounded work. Slow storage still limits throughput; adding database connections does not fix insufficient IOPS.

PostgreSQL requires correct POSIX filesystem semantics and reliable fsync. NFS requires a hard mount and a server export that preserves fsync durability. Do not disable fsync for speed. blks_hit measures PostgreSQL cache hits, not the entire OS cache. Use pg_stat_database and pg_stat_activity on PostgreSQL 14/15; pg_stat_io is available from 16. Official requirements: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/creating-cluster.html

sections.title: Setup order
sections.body:
1. [Create a profile](/dashboard/management/config-profiles) with a valid inbound and a unique tag.
2. [Connect a node](/dashboard/management/nodes), select the profile and activate the inbound.
3. [Create an internal squad](/dashboard/management/internal-squads) granting that inbound.
4. [Create a host](/dashboard/management/hosts) with its address and port, linked to the inbound.
5. [Create an active user](/dashboard/management/users), set expiry and add the squad.
6. Open the [user](/dashboard/management/users), copy their subscription URL and import it into a compatible client.

sections.title: If a host is missing
sections.body: Check squad membership, inbound activation on the node, host visibility/status, squad restrictions on the host and account status. Then check the delivered format and User-Agent response rules. A host existing in the panel does not prove that a particular user can access it.

sections.title: Moving around
sections.body: The sidebar expands categories. On a phone the menu button opens navigation, which closes after choosing a page. Quick launch finds sections; open entity resolves a known user, node, host or profile by identifier. Documentation links preserve the selected article or API operation in the URL.

sections.title: Tables and recipients
sections.body: Use search, column filters, sorting, page size and column visibility. Row selection and table filtering are different concepts: review the recipient count before a bulk action. In limits, ALL targets all current entitled users of the scope, not just the visible page or search results.

sections.title: Metrics
sections.body: Home shows transferred traffic, current bandwidth, online users and nodes, account status totals and activity statistics. Transferred volume and bandwidth are different quantities. Online now, online today/week and never online describe different time windows and should not be expected to match.

sections.title: Panel diagnostics
sections.body: Open a status card for details. If data has not appeared, wait for loading or refresh. A spinning icon indicates that the request is still in progress.

sections.title: Database diagnostics
sections.body:
Home shows application connections, active queries, lock waits and idle transactions. The snapshot covers only the current role and panel database; the diagnostics query excludes itself. SQL text, addresses and keys are not shown. An administrator session is required; API tokens cannot use this endpoint. Unknown statistics appear as “—”, not zero. A diagnostics failure leaves the other Home sections working.

The interface polls every 30 seconds in a visible tab; the server coalesces concurrent requests and retains a sample for 15 seconds per process. Total traffic charts also use a bounded 15-second snapshot. This display cache does not change access checks, quotas or blocks. Rising wait counts or query times call for log and SQL-plan inspection; a connection count alone does not prove overload.

sections.title: Identity and contacts
sections.body: The username identifies an account. Email, Telegram ID, description and tag help with searching and grouping. Internal squads determine connection access.

sections.title: Access and quota
sections.body: Set status, expiry, subscription traffic quota, reset strategy, internal squads and optionally an external squad. A subscription quota of 0 is unlimited. Host and tag quotas remain independent. The field reference below uses the exact names and help text from the current form.

sections.title: Saving
sections.body: Before saving, check squads and subscription expiry. Then verify the status and date in the detail view. A subscription ends at the specified time; the date indicator’s color does not change the expiry.

sections.title: How expiry is checked
sections.body: The panel scheduler enqueues an expiry check every 30 seconds in USERS_WATCHDOG_QUEUE. Overdue ACTIVE and LIMITED users become EXPIRED and node access is synchronized. No extra crontab is needed. The scheduler, queue worker, Valkey and database must be running; stopping a worker delays execution. FROZEN users are excluded from expiry: the saved remainder is expireAt minus frozenAt, and activation computes a new expiry from the current time. No continuous database date rewrite is required. Scheduled traffic resets follow their own schedule and never unfreeze users.

sections.title: Freeze a subscription
sections.body: Choose Freeze in the user menu: ordinary access is paused and the remaining lifetime is retained. Two days remaining stay two days until activation. Resuming sets the new expiry from that remainder; repeating Freeze does not change it. Zero remaining time or an exhausted quota does not grant access. Extending adds to the remainder. Expired subscriptions can be frozen with zero remaining time; the saved remainder is formatted independently of the current date. A blue saved remainder replaces the date editor. Active expiry warnings turn yellow at three days and red on expiry. Freezing itself does not reset usage; scheduled traffic resets continue. The state survives restarts and export/import. Bulk freezes synchronize each user’s device access through the queue.

sections.title: Device subscription preview
sections.body: Select an already registered device, format and User-Agent in the device card and generate a preview. It uses the real generator and response rules without changing the device or connection history or creating access keys in the database. A blocked device receives no working access. The host list shows candidates; the generator performs final protocol and pool filtering. Configuration containing keys is hidden by default and returned only on explicit request, up to 2 MiB. Treat it as private and keep it out of public logs.

sections.title: Status and resets
sections.body: ACTIVE allows access when other checks pass. DISABLED turns off the account, EXPIRED indicates expiry and LIMITED an exhausted subscription quota. Enable, disable, reset traffic and revoke/rotate a subscription are separate operations. Resetting subscription usage must not be treated as resetting every host/tag quota; use Limits for those scopes.

sections.title: Card buttons
sections.body: QR and connection keys help import the subscription. JSON shows data, metadata exposes extra properties, details show account information and nodes show placement/access. Other buttons open torrent restrictions, subscription request history, HWID devices and active connections. Tooltips and accessible button names identify actions; touch controls have larger hit areas.

sections.title: Link and deletion
sections.body: Click the subscription field or copy button to copy its URL. The adjacent help opens on click and works on phones. The URL contains the user access secret: do not publish a real link in documentation. Deleting removes the account; disabling keeps it available for later reactivation.

sections.title: Updating selected accounts
sections.body: Select users, choose an action and check the recipient count before confirming. In bulk editing, set only the fields you want to change. Each user keeps their other values. For example, changing the expiration date does not also change squads or the traffic quota.

sections.title: Checking results
sections.body: Squad, traffic, expiry, device and status changes affect each recipient. Review selection before deleting. Refresh after completion and inspect an individual account. A network failure does not prove that no operation ran: read the current state before retrying a mutation.

sections.title: Import format
sections.body: Upload an exported JSON file containing a users list with at most 20,000 records. “Restore squads by name” assigns users to existing internal squads with matching names; missing squads are not created. Turn it off to discard squad assignments from the file. The additional squad selected in the form is assigned to every imported user independently of this checkbox.

sections.title: What is transferred
sections.body: Check the created, skipped and failed counts after import. An existing username or short identifier causes a record to be skipped; other errors appear in the import result. Test a subscription belonging to a newly created user. The export contains access credentials: keep the file private. It is not a database backup and does not transfer profiles, nodes, API tokens or all panel settings.

sections.title: Limit and registration
sections.body: HWID is enabled by default on a new installation; an upgrade preserves the saved switch. A compatible app sends its device identifier when requesting a subscription. An empty user limit uses the shared fallback limit, 0 allows any number of devices, and a positive number sets the maximum. With a limit of 3, a fourth new device cannot register. “Disallow new devices” separately stops registration while preserving access for existing allowed devices.

sections.title: Deletion versus blocking
sections.body: Deleting a device removes its registration: the same app can register again if new devices are allowed. To prevent access, block it instead: the record remains and that device’s access is revoked. Unblocking removes the ban. “Delete all unblocked” clears allowed registrations while keeping blocked device records.

sections.title: Requirements
sections.body: The application must send supported HWID headers. Removing a registration is not a permanent admission ban. Automation uses separate registration, blocking and unblocking scopes; listing devices does not grant blocking permission.

sections.title: Purpose
sections.body: A squad groups allowed inbounds and its users. Create it, choose inbounds and assign users. A user can join multiple internal squads. Changing inbounds changes granted access; a squad does not create nodes or hosts automatically.

sections.title: Management
sections.body: The card opens members, inbound assignment, statistics and group actions. Exporting members transfers users rather than the entire squad infrastructure. Host squad restrictions may include or exclude a host, so membership alone does not guarantee every host appears in a subscription.

sections.title: Purpose
sections.body: An external squad supplies a subscription delivery variant for an assigned user, including templates, subscription page and supported overrides. It does not replace internal squads that authorize inbounds. Assign it only after reviewing the group settings.

sections.title: Overrides
sections.body: Changing external squad templates or settings can change delivery for all members. Compare an individual subscription with global settings because external squad overrides can affect the result. Verify delivery after deleting or changing the assigned group.

sections.title: Connection
sections.body:
A node is a server agent running our Xray. Create the record, set its management address/port, configure connection credentials and select a profile with active inbounds. The management port is separate from a host client port. Verify reachability from the panel server and correct connection parameters.

In card view, nodes can be dragged with a tag selected. Only visible nodes are reordered; other records keep their positions. Form actions stay at the bottom of the window while scrolling.

sections.title: Fields and accounting
sections.body: Name, country, tags and provider describe infrastructure. The profile and inbound list determine active services. A node consumption multiplier changes user traffic accounting and is not a bandwidth cap. Traffic tracking, monthly threshold, reset day and node notifications concern server usage rather than an individual user quota.

sections.title: Paused start queue
sections.body: Applying a profile in bulk does not pause the global start queue; operations are coordinated per node. An existing manual pause or one left by an older update is not automatically resumed. If jobs remain paused, confirm that maintenance is complete and resume the queue in Bull Board. Restarting the panel must not override an intentional administrative pause.

sections.title: Recovery after a core crash
sections.body: After a confirmed crash of a compatible core, the agent restores the last private configuration without the panel. A working process is left running; unknown status or busy management defers the check. Administrative pause and quota checks remain enforced. Automatic attempts are limited to three recoveries per hour of the agent process. A further crash after that limit or a recovery error stops retries; check the log, correct the cause and explicitly start a new process. Hot application of settings does not reset the attempt budget. A corrupt journal is never cleared. Both Node and Core builds must include this fix; updating only the panel does not replace them.

sections.title: Confirming node commands
sections.body: Start and stop operations for one node run sequentially. An outdated command must not overwrite a newer state or connection address. An unconfirmed stop retains its error and is retried up to five times, 30 seconds apart. A node disabled by an administrator is never automatically enabled after failure. Check connectivity and the log, then retry the action. An unavailable node can still be deleted from the panel. Bulk profile jobs run one at a time while retaining shared configuration preparation. Updating the Node image preserves the previously selected managed Core. Check the running version in Node tasks and update Core separately if needed, then refresh the client subscription. An outdated autoselect-limit warning clears after support and successful policy application are confirmed; a failed check never removes restrictions.

sections.title: Xray settings
sections.body:
Xray settings selects one core flavor for the entire panel. The default is the custom Remnacust core. Stock Xray supports standard protocols and transports. Users, freezing, subscriptions, geofiles and client-side autoselect work in both modes. Host/device limits, separate autoselect recipient accounting, destination access rules, inactive-access hosts, port plans and Xera HTTP require the custom core. Stock mode disables their controls and effective policies without deleting saved settings.

Before switching to stock Xray, the panel checks active profiles, port plans and quota journals. Resolve the listed blockers; never delete accounting data or reserves merely to switch. Dual-core selection on a custom node requires an updated Node image; native Remnawave nodes retain baseline compatibility. Changes are queued and the scheduler retries delivery if the queue is temporarily unavailable. Selection does not prove every node applied it: check node status.

Switching cores restarts the core and may interrupt connections. Save editor changes first. An open editor refreshes on a mode change and loads the matching validator and schema. The global choice overrides the legacy geodata.core profile selector without rewriting the saved profile. Custom core version management is available only in custom mode.

sections.title: Installation and certificates
sections.body: SSH installation requires root or passwordless sudo; an existing empty directory is allowed. Failures show the stage and detailed logs remain on the server. With a panel-IP restriction and HTTP-01, TCP 80 opens temporarily for certificate validation and closes afterwards; a failed process cannot keep it open longer than 15 minutes. Renewal uses the same rule. External and provider firewalls need their own configuration. Use DNS-01 or an existing certificate to keep port 80 closed.

sections.title: Diagnostics and safe operations
sections.body:
Diagnostics make a real mTLS request to the registered node and check Xray, user synchronization and port apply status. They do not verify the full client network path. Disabled nodes are not probed; manual probes are rate limited. Port edits are reviewed, then confirmed with a review hash and current revision: stale reviews are rejected. Success requires node ACK, not merely enqueueing. Errors allow restoring a previously applied revision without overwriting newer edits. Outages require three observations over at least 20 seconds; recovery requires two over 10 seconds. Never-connected installations do not generate outage alerts. Maintenance and operations suppress alerts; a manual 30-minute pause does not stop health checks. The install wizard uses the verified installer over SSH and confirms connectivity separately; existing directories are not overwritten. NET_ADMIN defaults off. When a main server IP is set, all incoming ports and ping accept only that source except SSH (22 and detected sshd ports). Rules cover Docker forwarding and IPv6, preserve outbound replies and never flush other firewall rules. This blocks external HTTP-01 renewals: use DNS-01 or externally managed certificates. Remove the guard with python3 /etc/remnacust-node-firewall/guard.py remove.

Release checking (--check-release) does not run APT. Background component updates from the panel defer OS maintenance that requires SSH and record it in progress and the private log; that deferral alone does not block the component update. Maintain OS packages separately through an interactive SSH session and answer dpkg/debconf questions. --yes does not supply those answers; there is no automatic reboot.

sections.title: MPTCP and Linux kernel security
sections.body: Xray v26.10.31 disables MPTCP by default; explicit streamSettings.sockopt.tcpMptcp remains available. Restore earlier MPTCP behavior only after installing a patched Linux kernel and booting that kernel. A Docker image does not update the host kernel. CVE-2026-98432 affects IPv4 TCP: disabling MPTCP reduces attack surface but does not fix the kernel bug itself. Verify the exact distribution package against its security bulletin rather than relying only on uname -r. Inspect listeners with sudo ss -Mlnp. Do not enable MPTCP on an unverified kernel. Sources: https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-core/releases/tag/v26.10.31 and https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/PCoQcdxoScw/m/aD-MgXEvAAAJ.

sections.title: Enable, restart and reset
sections.body: Enable/disable controls the node state in the panel. Restart reapplies Xray operation and can interrupt connections. Resetting usage statistics does not delete users or upgrade the core. Deleting a node record does not terminate the provider server.

sections.title: Bulk update
sections.body: Selecting multiple nodes shows the changed fields in confirmation. Before switching profiles, verify certificates, listen addresses and ports on each server. After applying, inspect health on every selected node rather than only the first row.

sections.title: Changing an active port
sections.body: Compatible changes apply through the core without restarting its process. From Node 1.1.21, an ordinary profile update with the exact native port-or-transport rejection validates the configuration and automatically restarts Xray only. Failed startup restores the previous private checkpoint and working configuration. Connections may briefly drop. Timeouts, unknown replies and damaged checkpoints do not authorize automatic restart. Strict requireLiveApply and managed port plans retain their contract: such a rejection never becomes a hidden full restart. Updating the container or core binary can also interrupt connections.

sections.title: State and resources
sections.body:
Open a node card to inspect connectivity, online users, CPU load, memory, networking and Xray information. Available metrics depend on the agent. A missing value does not mean zero load: check connectivity and refresh. Panel, node agent and Xray versions are listed separately under Documentation → Versions.

Host policies could not be applied. The new configuration was not sent to the node; a running Xray keeps its previous configuration. Check host isolation v2 support in the node and core. The panel will retry once support is restored. The configured limits remain enabled.

Update the node to Remnacust Node 1.1.1 with our Xray. This profile requires host isolation v2. Its limits and new connections will not work until the update. The running configuration is kept; after updating, the panel will apply the new one automatically.

Use MANAGEMENT or RESERVE roles for control addresses. OUTBOUND, BLOCKED and other roles do not make an address a control fallback candidate. Every candidate keeps the same configured node API port; other ports are not scanned. Use diagnostics to check connectivity: the panel backend sends an authenticated request to the node API. An open TCP port, a DNS answer or an old green status does not confirm it. Check the observation time and repeat the check after changing settings. The primary address and explicitly configured fallback IPs receive an authenticated API check. The administrator must enter only addresses of the same node: shared TLS/JWT credentials establish panel trust, not a unique node UUID. This check cannot distinguish another node using the same trusted keys or CA. No external address discovery is performed.

Proxy URL affects only the panel → node control channel, not user VPN traffic. The field is masked by default; reveal it to inspect or edit the URL. If SOCKS5 is configured, every candidate uses that same proxy. Changing the node IP cannot fix an unavailable shared proxy; there is no silent direct fallback. Explicitly leave Proxy URL empty to select a direct connection. Route status must not display the username, password or raw proxy URL. Node responses to API tokens, including wildcard tokens, return proxyUrl: null to avoid exposing SOCKS credentials. Administrator sessions retain the setting in the masked editor; route status does not expose the password. SOCKS5 username/password authentication under RFC 1929 sends the username and password to the proxy in plaintext. Use a trusted proxy over a private network or a protected tunnel. The Node API channel remains encrypted with mTLS; it does not encrypt the separate SOCKS5 handshake. [RFC 1929](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1929.html#section-3).

sections.title: Logs
sections.body: The health log helps locate connection failures, application errors and restarts. The Xray log shows core messages; its contents depend on logging settings. Compare message timestamps with profile changes.

sections.title: How node health is calculated
sections.body: Disabled, disconnected or still connecting nodes show 0/100. Missing active profile/inbounds or fresh running-Xray confirmation also gives zero. Once these prerequisites hold, each of four signals contributes 25 points: configuration, connection, running core and normal resources. Missing metrics never inflate the result. Cached metrics of disconnected nodes are not presented as current. Unknown data, memory pressure and sustained CPU load are listed separately. Resource cache lasts 30 seconds and Xray uptime 16 seconds; expiry removes confirmation without proving a core crash.

sections.title: Server access
sections.body: The terminal connects using separately configured SSH credentials. Its address and port may differ from the node agent. Commands run on the selected server as the SSH user; sudo depends on server permissions. Verify the target node before running commands.

sections.title: Access
sections.body: The SSH terminal supports administrative server work. Closing a tab does not guarantee that commands stop. Check the result and status of a long-running operation before starting it again.

sections.title: Optimization levels
sections.body: none, safe, balanced and performance launch the bundled script through the SSH terminal. They change server OS settings rather than subscription limits. Recommendations use memory: below 2 GiB or at least 85% memory usage suggests safe; other servers suggest balanced.

sections.title: Verifying application
sections.body: Check reads the actual server state. A chosen level can differ from the last verified level until the command and verification finish. If verification fails, do not assume success: inspect SSH output.

sections.title: Choosing an update
sections.body: In node tasks, choose Install release and a verified build. The panel includes a current catalog for amd64 and arm64 and selects a build automatically. Refresh reloads the list. An empty or unavailable catalog shows an explanation and prevents installation; the bundled core remains a separate action. Update both the panel and nodes to use the default public catalog. Switching may temporarily interrupt connections.

sections.title: Operation result
sections.body: Follow the task status and each node’s log. Where available, cancellation applies to a task still in progress. After completion, check the core version, node health and a test user connection. Host and tag limits and device revocation require a compatible core.

sections.title: Plugin configuration
sections.body: The beta section stores plugin configurations, tags and node assignments. Create, clone, edit, delete, reorder and synchronize are distinct actions. The editor validates configuration and warns before leaving with unsaved changes. Saving is separate from executor operation.

sections.title: Shared lists
sections.body: Shared lists let multiple configurations reference the same list. Synchronize after editing and check assigned nodes. Deleting or renaming a referenced list can affect several plugins.

sections.title: After core startup
sections.body: The postStart section in plugin JSON runs enabled actions after Xray starts or restarts. To send a notification, enable postStart.enabled and postStart.webhook.enabled and set webhook.url. The node sends a POST containing service.core_started, a timestamp and its metadata. Delivery runs in the background with a five-second timeout; failures are logged without stopping Xray. Verify the destination before enabling it.

sections.title: Usage history
sections.body: Statistics show node usage across time ranges. Compare matching intervals. Instant bandwidth is not daily volume; resetting a monthly counter is not equivalent to deleting all historical records.

sections.title: Metrics
sections.body: The metrics page compares node load and health. An unreachable node may not return fresh values. Dates and available history depend on stored data and retention settings; the interface cannot reconstruct missing records.

sections.title: Server accounting
sections.body: Create a provider and assign nodes. Set cost and payment date/period using the available fields. Cards and statistics summarize infrastructure spending. The provider badge is accounting metadata rather than server authentication.

sections.title: Dates and notifications
sections.body: Payment dates help track renewal. Dates use UTC calendar days: more than 7 days is neutral, 2–7 days is yellow, tomorrow is orange, and today or overdue is red. Overdue totals are also red. Text distinguishes due today from overdue and shows the day count. Colors adapt to the theme, and statuses update at day changes and when returning to the tab. On phones, amounts and labels wrap, actions stay separate from long node names, and the last card can scroll clear of the bottom toolbar. Recording payment or editing a date in the panel does not transfer money to the provider. Check linked nodes and accounting history before deleting a provider.

sections.title: Server profile
sections.body: A profile contains the complete Xray configuration. Create it with uniquely tagged inbounds, outbounds, routing and DNS. Activate inbounds on nodes and grant them through squads. Hosts reference an inbound of that profile, so changing or removing its tag affects linked hosts.

sections.title: Save and clone
sections.body: Cloning creates a separate profile for experiments; editing the original can affect every assigned node. Server validation is independent of editor validation. Check node health after applying and avoid static accounts in place of panel-managed accounts.

sections.title: Recovering unsaved edits
sections.body:
In profile and subscription-template editors, open History → Unsaved draft. This contains the most recent local text, including incomplete JSON or YAML. Compare it with the saved version, choose Load into editor, then save normally. Nothing is applied automatically.

A successful save removes its temporary copy. Edits typed while that request is pending remain recoverable. A failed save does not delete the copy. Delete in this tab removes only the local draft.

Copies are separated by administrator and document. They are available only in this browser on this panel origin, for up to seven days and 8 MiB per document. Clearing site data removes them. Text is encrypted in IndexedDB; this does not protect an open administrator session. Storage restrictions or exceeded limits are shown as errors. Before a forced interface refresh, the interface waits for draft persistence. A browser crash can lose recent keystrokes that have not yet been written.

sections.title: Certificate files
sections.body: If the panel needs to read a PEM file while preparing configuration, mount it read-only under /var/lib/remnawave and use that path. Reads outside this directory, including symlink escapes, are denied. Ordinary text files, FIFOs and PEM files over 128 KiB are rejected. This applies to files read by the panel; it does not relocate node certificates or configure node HTTPS automatically.

sections.title: X25519 password and private key
sections.body: The generator shows two values: Private key for the server and Password (public key) for the REALITY client. For X25519, password and publicKey identify the same bytes, so no duplicate field is shown. Copy all contains privateKey and password. Do not distribute the private key to clients.

sections.title: Editing a configuration
sections.body: Open a profile and edit its JSON. Press Ctrl+Space for suggestions, use the up and down arrows to select an option, Enter to insert it or Esc to close the list. The current option is highlighted. Search, formatting and full-screen mode are also available. Before saving, fix marked errors and run configuration validation.

sections.title: Generate a shortId
sections.body: The Short ID tab in Tools generates 16 hex characters from 8 secure random bytes. Copy the value into shortIds in the server realitySettings and use the same value as shortId on the client. Generate creates a new value without changing the saved profile or starting rotation.

sections.title: Checks before applying
sections.body: Save validates JSON first. A missing protocol, a typo in it or a structural error produces an explanation without changing the profile or its history. If the built-in Xray validator reports another error, the panel displays it and asks you to confirm saving. Confirmation does not bypass server-side structural checks. A saved invalid profile can be reopened and corrected.

sections.title: After saving
sections.body: Database persistence and node application are separate steps. A queued message means a job was submitted; check node status and logs for its outcome. If queuing fails, the profile has still been saved and the panel shows a warning. Edits made while saving remain in the editor. Clone a profile first when preparing a separate variant.

sections.title: X25519 keys
sections.body: The X25519 tab in Tools shows password, publicKey and privateKey with separate copy buttons. password and publicKey contain the same public key; the names are used by different versions and clients. Set the private key on the REALITY server and the public key in the field supported by the client. All values copies the three fields. Generating updates them together without changing the saved profile.

sections.title: Origin and place in a connection
sections.body:
Xera HTTP is a fork of the XHTTP (SplitHTTP) transport from Xray-core, developed in Remnacust Core. It carries connection data in HTTP requests and responses. The original XHTTP implementation is in [Xray-core](https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-core/tree/v26.9.30/transport/internet/splithttp); our fork is in [xerahttp](https://github.com/lottman/Remnacust-core/tree/main/xray/transport/internet/xerahttp).

In a profile, VLESS specifies the connection protocol and user, Xera HTTP specifies the transport, and TLS or REALITY protects the connection. Thus protocol: "vless", streamSettings.network: "xera-http" and streamSettings.security: "tls" can be used together. When switching to Xera, do not replace protocol with xera-http; change the transport and its options inside streamSettings. TLS, the user UUID and routing retain their separate roles.

sections.title: Changes in the fork
sections.body:
Xera is registered separately as network: "xera-http" with xeraHttpSettings. Standard XHTTP remains a separate transport. The fork includes stream-auto, customDownlinkPadding for data blocks, configuration validation and resource limits for sessions, upload queues, headers and blocks. Session identifiers use a cryptographic random generator and are checked for allowed characters and sufficient entropy.

Request padding xPaddingBytes and customDownlinkPadding serve different purposes: the latter pads transmitted data blocks and needs compatible processing on both ends. Shared XHTTP ancestry does not mean every XHTTP client understands these extensions. Speed and reliability depend on the network, mode, proxy and settings; the fork alone does not promise faster connections or guaranteed circumvention.

sections.title: Compatibility
sections.body: Xera HTTP is an XHTTP fork in our Xray core. Both the node core and the client application core must support it. XHTTP support in a regular Xray build does not imply Xera support. Check that both builds accept network: "xera-http". Clone a working profile and test a separate host before changing it for all users.

sections.title: Profile configuration
Node, host and subscription
sections.body: Activate the inbound on a compatible node, permit it in an internal squad and link a [host](/dashboard/management/hosts). Set the public address, port and SNI on the host. Path and Host fields can override profile values for the client; they must match what the server or proxy accepts. Refresh a test user subscription. Xray JSON retains xeraHttpSettings; share links carry type=xera-http and xeraSettings. The client must understand this format. Sing-box, Clash and Mihomo generators skip these hosts because they do not support this transport.

sections.title: Modes and HTTP proxies
sections.body:
Start with mode: "auto". In our implementation it selects packet-up without REALITY; with REALITY it selects stream-one, or stream-up when separate downloadSettings are configured. A server using auto accepts supported client modes.

- packet-up: upload is split into finite HTTP requests; download uses a separate stream.
- stream-up: upload and download use separate long-running streaming requests.
- stream-one: upload and download share one bidirectional streaming request.
- stream-auto: for HTTP/2 with REALITY, selects stream-one or stream-up with downloadSettings; otherwise selects packet-up. HTTP/2 support at a CDN edge does not establish that the CDN forwards request bodies without buffering.

Upload in headers or cookies and GET require explicit packet-up. Match path, host and customized header options on both ends. The HTTP host and TLS SNI are distinct settings; specify Host through host, not headers.Host.

Behind an HTTP proxy, check the route, headers, request-body limits and timeouts. Streaming modes require forwarding request bodies before completion and unbuffered responses. REALITY needs the protected connection to reach the core; ordinary CDN TLS termination does not replace it. If the proxy cannot forward a mode, test packet-up on a separate host.

stream-auto remains available: it selects a mode from HTTP/REALITY and downloadSettings; it does not measure DPI, latency or buffering, and does not change an open stream after a network error.

sections.title: Additional traffic padding
sections.body:
customDownlinkPadding adds random bytes to transmitted blocks and increases traffic usage. Start without it. When enabled, set matching header and token values on both sides: header must start with X- and contain 3–64 characters; token must contain 16–128 base64url characters. Avoid reserved proxy headers. bytes accepts 0–1024 and blockBytes 1024–16384; budgetPercent caps overhead (up to 100%), burstBytes is the initial allowance (up to 1 MiB), and uplink enables upload padding. These settings do not replace TLS/REALITY or guarantee that a connection bypasses blocking.

bytes and blockBytes accept a number or a "from-to" range. budgetPercent: 0 or an omitted field disables the percentage cap, not padding itself. Set budgetPercent from 1 to 100 to constrain overhead. burstBytes requires a nonzero budget; the initial allowance may yield a higher percentage on a short connection. token coordinates padding processing; it does not replace the user UUID, protocol password or TLS. Leave padding disabled for the first test.

With a nonzero budgetPercent and zero or omitted burstBytes, the core uses a 4096-byte initial allowance. The budget concerns padding bytes; HTTP headers, TLS and framing also consume traffic.

sections.title: Verify the result
sections.body:
Validate JSON in the editor and save the profile. Database persistence and application on a node are separate stages: check the queue, node status and logs. Download the subscription again and compare network, path, mode and SNI in the client configuration. “Unknown transport” means the selected core does not support Xera. If the host is missing, check squads, access, filters and subscription format. For unstable connections, return to auto without additional padding and change one option at a time.

To migrate from XHTTP, clone the profile and host and keep the working configuration. Change streamSettings.network from xhttp to xera-http in the intended inbound and move verified xhttpSettings options to xeraHttpSettings. Do not change protocol, UUID, port or TLS/REALITY without a separate reason. Do not retain both settings blocks in the same variant. Renaming alone cannot give a standard XHTTP core Xera support: check both cores and the configuration the client actually imported. Start with the previous path and host, mode: "auto" and no new extensions. Verify connection, upload, download, reconnection and node logs before switching other users. To revert, use the saved XHTTP profile and refresh the subscription.

For a parallel test, use a separate node or a free port. Two inbounds must not listen on the same address and port at the same time.

sections.title: New wire profile and HTTP/2
sections.body:
Update the client and server cores together. Remove xPaddingObfsMode, noGRPCHeader, noSSEHeader and xPaddingMethod: "repeat-x": these settings are rejected. Tokenish padding always applies to requests and accepted transport responses. Padding, session and sequence placement must match on both peers; legacy locations are not searched. uplinkHTTPMethod must also match. OPTIONS carrying Access-Control-Request-Method and Origin is a browser preflight; OPTIONS without that header can carry upload data.

h2Params configures the HTTP/2 server, for example {"MaxConcurrentStreams":128,"MaxReadFrameSize":65536}. Unknown fields, prohibited ciphers and invalid sizes are rejected; timeouts are numeric nanoseconds. This does not configure a browser fingerprint for the HTTP/2 client.

Headers follow the TLS ClientHello family; explicit values take priority. Unrecognized requests receive the same ordinary 404 response before session allocation or body reads. Padding and these responses do not replace TLS/REALITY or VLESS. uTLS does not mimic the entire browser HTTP/2/QUIC stack. An ISP cannot read HTTP inside HTTPS, but a CDN terminating TLS can. DPI indistinguishability is not guaranteed: comparative measurements on the target network are required.

Transport HTTP header names must start with X-, contain 3–64 characters and avoid proxy headers. Session, sequence and padding keys sharing a placement must be distinct. Invalid or conflicting settings are rejected before starting the listener.

Tokenish padding is now generated in one pass from random Base62 symbols with an exact HPACK Huffman-encoded size, without a deterministic repair suffix. This is the size of the padding value, not the complete HTTP request or TLS packet.

When the server enables customDownlinkPadding, every request requires exactly one matching header/token marker and the client verifies the response acknowledgement. Missing, incorrect or repeated markers receive an ordinary 404 before body reads or session allocation; there is no unpadded fallback. Update both ends together. Browser Dialer does not support this extension, so CORS preflights are also rejected for it. Generate token from 32 random bytes encoded as base64url. The marker is shared by the profile and visible to a TLS-terminating CDN and profile users: it does not replace VLESS authorization or stop a participant who already knows it.

sections.title: Camouflage limits and measurement
sections.body:
Encryption hides content, but not the server address, packet sizes, directions or timing. Matching HTTP headers alone does not reproduce browser behavior. TLS-in-TLS and The Parrot Is Dead describe limitations; results for other tunnels do not measure our Xera. FRONT studies cover traffic in a Tor model, so its settings cannot be transferred without measurements.

Evaluate passive classification and active requests separately. Compare ordinary HTTPS and Xera captures on the same network across workloads and session lengths; measure false positives, latency, traffic overhead, CPU and memory. H1/H2/H3 functional and race tests establish correctness, not DPI indistinguishability. This local change adds no background requests, artificial delays or live protocol switching.

[TLS-in-TLS, USENIX 2024](https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity24/presentation/xue-fingerprinting) · [The Parrot Is Dead](https://dedis.cs.yale.edu/dissent/papers/parrot-abs/) · [FRONT](https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity20/presentation/gong) · [Security Engineering, 20.4](https://www.cl.cam.ac.uk/archive/rja14/Papers/SEv3-ch20.pdf)

sections.title: Client HTTP/2 wire profile
sections.body:
The new local client path aligns the HTTP/2 opening with the supported Chrome 133 TLS profile: SETTINGS and their order, pseudo-header order, connection window and header compression. It is selected automatically for chrome, hellochrome_133 and an empty fingerprint while the pinned uTLS maps them to Chrome 133. Other versions and families retain the standard H2 path, with no browser-equivalence claim. This change does not alter HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/3.

This is HTTP/2 behavior inside the protected connection, not new encryption. An ISP cannot read SETTINGS inside TLS; a TLS-terminating CDN can. Alignment removes one specific cross-layer mismatch, but does not hide the server address, session duration or application traffic patterns. Full DPI indistinguishability has not been established.

TLS/REALITY, certificate verification, certificate pinning and ALPN checks remain in the existing Xray path. Redirects are not followed, changing HTTP authority in one transport is rejected, and POST requests are not automatically replayed after an error. Request cancellation, closure and connection reuse are supported. Each client transport permits at most four connections and 32 active HTTP requests per direction; waiting requests honor their own cancellation context. No background requests or artificial delays are added.

The path uses pinned fhttp v0.7.3. A loopback test checks the actual transmitted frames, not just configuration values. This is a local change and does not establish that a release has been published.

Before HTTP/2 decoding, response boundaries are checked: frames cannot exceed the advertised 16 KiB; a header block is limited to 512 KiB and 32 frames and must complete within 10 seconds. An invalid CONTINUATION sequence closes the connection. The deadline is cleared after headers complete and does not limit data-transfer duration. This bounds excessive header processing without changing payloads or encryption.

sections.title: Checking options in the editor
sections.body:
Node profiles and Xray subscription templates use the same transport schema. Completions also cover extra, customDownlinkPadding, xmux and downloadSettings. The editor checks supported values and bounds; WASM additionally runs the configuration builder. Valid JSON alone does not establish application support.

After changing the core, rebuild the editor and frontend. Schemas, WASM and its JavaScript each receive a content-based URL version, so updated completions do not redownload unchanged WASM.

h2Params and server resource limits stay on the node and are omitted from client subscriptions, including inside extra. Shared transport options and downloadSettings are preserved. xmux.hKeepAlivePeriod is in seconds: 0 selects the default, -1 disables idle probes, and positive values cannot exceed 604800. HTTP header names and values are checked before startup. Set Host through the separate host field.

sections.title: Canvas and JSON
sections.body: The canvas helps visualize a profile’s inbounds, outbounds and routes. Open the desired profile and compare edits with JSON. Applied JSON remains the core configuration: visual block placement alone does not determine rule order.

sections.title: Checking changes
sections.body: Validate and save profile edits, then inspect assigned node health. Review complex parameters in the JSON editor when the canvas does not expose them; an absent visual block is not a reason to remove its JSON parameter.

sections.title: Reusable configuration
sections.body: A snippet stores a named configuration fragment. Create it, use it in profiles and edit it centrally. Saving the fragment and synchronizing its consumers are distinct steps; synchronization confirmation distributes the change.

sections.title: Deletion
sections.body: The interface offers synchronization after deleting a snippet. Check affected profiles and nodes because references may need changes. Validate the resulting JSON before broad application, not only the isolated fragment.

sections.title: Key material
sections.body: The generator creates supported key pairs and configuration parameters. Public keys can be delivered to clients; private keys must remain server-side. Formats for different protocols are not interchangeable. Preserve matching parts and check the key against the selected inbound.

sections.title: Shadowsocks-2022
sections.body: Choose the key type matching the cipher in your Shadowsocks-2022 configuration. Use matching parameters on the server and client. Keys for different ciphers are not interchangeable.

sections.title: Core parameters
sections.body:
Remark names a subscription connection. Address and port are the client endpoint; inbound supplies server parameters from a profile. SNI, Host, path, ALPN and security customize TLS/transport and must match the server. Host node assignment and node inbound activation are separate settings.

Above the list, choose Enabled, Disabled, Visible or Hidden. Visible includes hosts with isHidden = false, including disabled hosts. Enabled includes hosts with isDisabled = false, including hidden hosts. The filter combines with the selected tag in card and table views. In card view, drag hosts within a tag; other records keep their positions. Save, copy and delete actions remain available at the bottom of the form while scrolling.

sections.title: Visibility and actions
sections.body:
A hidden host is omitted from new subscription responses, but hiding alone does not revoke credentials already issued. Disabling a host controls access through node policy. Internal squads restrict who receives the host. Cloning creates another host record with the original settings; it does not create a server. After saving, wait for policy application and test a user’s subscription.

If the panel loses contact with a node, an authorized host remains in the subscription with the same connection details. Node health alone does not hide it. The connection may fail until the server recovers; once it recovers, a subscription refresh is not needed just to restore the host entry. Visibility, disabled status, squad restrictions, quotas and device blocks are checked separately.

sections.title: Bulk editing
sections.body: Select hosts, choose the fields to update and check the recipients. Selecting the tags field and leaving it empty clears tags; leaving the field unselected preserves existing tags. Record order determines subscription order except where shuffling is enabled. After changing an inbound, visibility or squad, refresh the subscription in a client and check that the intended connection is present.

sections.title: Restricted host latency
sections.body: An HTTP check must reach an allowed website through the host itself. In Allow only mode, the form shows a copyable URL for the first allowed domain. For Happ with a real Provider ID, the panel selects a common allowed URL for all delivered visible hosts, preserving a suitable configured URL and HTTP method. Explicit TCP and ICMP choices are unchanged. When no shared domain exists or only IP/CIDR destinations are allowed, it falls back to TCP; TCP confirms server reachability, not VPN authorization. In INCY, choose HTTP/INCY ping and this URL in subscription settings: ordinary HTTP headers cannot set its probe URL; automatic configuration requires INCY’s own Premium API. Website permissions are not widened and the check never goes through DIRECT. The website must respond to the selected HTTP method; redirects to a denied domain remain blocked.

sections.title: Dynamic device bandwidth
sections.body: The user speed in Mbps is a shared ceiling for all their connections on this host. Active device keys share it by bytes served: one device uses available capacity; when another sends traffic, capacity is redistributed. Idle devices reserve nothing. The device speed limit caps all connections of its private key, combining upload and download. With a 20 Mbps user ceiling and a 15 Mbps device ceiling, one active device gets up to 15 Mbps; two continuously demanding devices can share 20 Mbps, roughly 10 Mbps each. These are ceilings, not guaranteed network rates. A configured host or tag shared ceiling is divided first among users, then their devices; opening more flows does not increase the share. Without a configured shared ceiling the core does not know the physical channel capacity.

sections.title: One user’s speed
sections.body: Under “For each user on this host”, set the quota in GiB and speed in Mbps. These are different limits: quota is a data allowance, speed is the transfer rate. All devices and connections of one user on this host share the speed, including upload and download. With 2 Mbps, two devices together get up to 2 Mbps; another user has a separate allowance. Another host uses its own setting. 0 disables only the host’s own cap; enabled tag restrictions remain. Shared speed for all host users and the accounting multiplier appear below.

sections.title: Bulk actions and country search
sections.body: Enable, disable and delete return after the database commit; node policy delivery starts in the background and unavailable nodes are retried. A saved action does not mean a disconnected node already received it. Buttons show progress and the list updates after API acknowledgement. Cloning runs at most three requests at once; successful sources are deselected and failed sources remain for retry. Search flags by country name in RU/EN/FA/ZH or two-letter code independently of the UI language.

sections.title: TLS, transport and client
sections.body: SNI specifies the TLS name; overrideSniFromAddress derives it from the address, and fingerprint configures client TLS. Host and path are transport fields. Certificate pinning, verifyPeerCertByName, Mihomo X25519 and IP version require compatible clients. Verify format support before transferring mux, sockopt, transport JSON overrides or serverDescription settings.

sections.title: Domain rules
sections.body: OFF disables the additional filter. ALLOW_ONLY permits only listed destinations, while DENY blocks them. This is a host traffic policy rather than a User-Agent subscription delivery condition. Verify required DNS/service destinations and inbound isolation support.

sections.title: SNI and shortId rotation
sections.body: Rotation uses the configured SNI pool and hourly interval; shortIds rotate when enabled. Form ranges are 1–8760 hours, 1–10 shortIds and length 4–16. Nodes apply updated settings and clients need a refreshed subscription. Do not enable rotation without a valid pool and compatible server configuration.

sections.title: Tag and policy
sections.body: A tag groups hosts but does not create a quota by itself: configure and save the tag settings. Each host independently opts into tag quota, per-user bandwidth and shared bandwidth. These switches are independent, and host-specific limits still apply alongside enabled tag limits.

sections.title: Bandwidth and multiplier
sections.body: Tag quota combines a user’s usage across participating hosts. A tag per-user bandwidth cap applies independently on each participating host; shared tag bandwidth is shared across participating traffic. An explicit host multiplier controls accounting, while null selects tag inheritance; the host’s own quota then uses multiplier 1 as explained by the form.

sections.title: Persistent settings
sections.body: Tag settings affect associated hosts with the corresponding quota, user-speed or shared-speed switch enabled. The device-speed inheritance switch is also independent. Check participating hosts and restrictions before saving. Open “Limits” for recipients and personal exceptions.

sections.title: Traffic accounting and quota batches
sections.body: Pending traffic commits at most eight receipts per transaction. A receipt may contain several users. Redis acknowledgements are removed after PostgreSQL commits, and retries do not charge usage twice. Fresh counter collection remains locked until its result is saved. Quota epochs are written in batches of up to 500 rows within the revision transaction. The coordinator commits funding and its cursor per owner, checks the generation and renews its lease between scopes. The budget is checked between owners; one owner with many scopes may take longer than 20 seconds.

sections.title: Device speed from tags
sections.body: A tag device ceiling applies independently on each host with “Apply device speed limit from tags” enabled. It is independent of tag quota, user speed and shared speed. The strictest applicable ceiling wins; 0 disables only the corresponding ceiling. Update node and core to support remnacust-device-speed-v1. An incompatible node cannot confirm the new limit. Across multiple bound nodes, the configured ceiling is conservatively divided so their sum cannot exceed it; spare capacity is not transferred between nodes. HWID enrolls a distinct private key. Copies of one key count as one device; applications without distinct keys cannot identify physical devices separately. Local rules remain active while the panel is unavailable.

sections.title: Speed by tag
sections.body: A tag’s user speed sets the same cap separately on each participating host. Shared group speed is a separate pool for all participating traffic. Each host independently enables the tag quota, user speed and shared speed. When several restrictions apply, the stricter cap wins. 0 means no corresponding cap, not blocked traffic. Mbps already means megabits per second; 8 Mbps is approximately 1 MB/s before overhead.

sections.title: Formats
sections.body: Xray JSON, Mihomo, Stash, Singbox and Clash have separate templates. Choose a format/template and edit its structure. A client template is different from a server Xray profile. The generator inserts allowed hosts and user data; formats without protocol support may exclude incompatible hosts.

sections.title: Checking delivery
sections.body: Create or select a template for the required format. When renaming it, choose a name not already used by another template of that format. If the name exists, the panel marks the field and explains the error while keeping your input. Before deleting a template, check subscription settings and external squads that use it. After editing, fetch a test user’s subscription and import it into the client: valid JSON or YAML does not verify a connection.

sections.title: Selection by total HTTP response time
sections.body:
Lowest response time (ping + TTFB) selects by an HTTP probe through each pool server. Xray uses leastPing with observatory or burstObservatory; Mihomo/Clash/Stash use url-test and sing-box uses urltest. The user app measures the route, not the panel. Timing includes connection setup, TLS for HTTPS and waiting for the HTTP response. It is not separate ICMP ping or a sum of two independently measured values.

For leastPing, the panel supplies a missing observer and enrolls every balancer selector in HTTP checks, including hand-written JSON. Custom URLs, intervals and explicit HTTP methods are preserved. Defaults are https://www.gstatic.com/generate_204 and 30s; burstObservatory uses HEAD, a 5s timeout and sampling 2. HEAD does not download the response body; an explicit burstObservatory GET includes reading the body in its delay. Choose the same small response, preferably 204, reachable through the entire pool. Measuring from the panel cannot bypass a blocked probe site.

After initial measurements, the app refreshes results on its configured interval. New connections use the current selection without refreshing the subscription; existing streams do not move. Burst uses the sample mean; native url-test/urltest tolerance reduces frequent switching. Probe settings and supported values depend on the client core. Probe timeout and fallback configure failure behavior. Pool membership still respects user access and applicable quotas.

sections.title: Autoselect in code and UI
sections.body: The Xray JSON Editing and Autoselect tabs share one draft. Editing an existing pool or balancer immediately updates its JSON. A new pool adds injectHosts, a balancer, routing and observation for leastPing or leastLoad. Adding a balancer for the same pool again does not create a second card. An unfinished balancer named after its pool is completed in place. Created and copied templates appear in the list immediately. Other outbounds, rules and settings remain intact. The changes panel compares against the last save; on phones it appears below the form. Save publishes a valid draft; text with errors is saved on the server with warnings and remains available in history.

sections.title: Host pools and tags
sections.body: selector.type supports uuids, exact tags, tagRegex, remarkRegex and sameTagAsRecipient. All support all/random/group; tag groups contain tags, other groups contain eligible host UUIDs. mode all injects all eligible sources, random selects at most selector.expected unique hosts, and group chooses one nonempty eligible group from selector.groups. Groups can be a named object or an array of arrays. Missing mode keeps legacy all; missing selectFrom selects hidden hosts. Access, visibility and exclusions are checked before selection. Recipient and source quotas are separate. Sampling occurs when a subscription is generated, not for each VPN connection. A profile with an explicit mode and no eligible sources is omitted.

sections.title: Assignment and balancing
sections.body: In Where to use autoselect, choose a specific selection and its recipients. remnawave.assignments contains balancerTag and a recipient list. In the GUI, choose Hosts or Tags first; only that list is shown. Switching mode removes the other list from this assignment. Existing mixed assignments show a warning and change only after an explicit choice. Direct host assignment beats a tag match; an explicit template in the host card beats another template. One host can receive multiple autoselects, each as a separate profile. Repeated tag matches do not duplicate profiles. Quota and speed are configured on the recipient host. Autoselect does not debit pool members or inherit their speed limits. Multiple autoselects for one recipient share its allowance. Without recipient limits or enabled recipient tag limits, autoselect has no host-level ceiling. The account quota still applies. Source pools remain limited by user access. Renaming or deleting a balancer updates its assignments. Legacy assignTo remains readable; choose its selection when editing. The card menu can duplicate any supported template format: settings, draft, tags and geofile references are preserved, while recipient assignments are cleared. Save remains available with code errors; invalid content stays a draft. Error paths identify the pool and reveal its field in code. The failed-probe fraction tolerance is between 0 and 1: 0.01 means 1%. Zero disables this check. A numeric value outside 0–1 is preserved in JSON; Xray clamps it internally when reading the configuration (for example, 2 becomes 1).

sections.title: Autoselect limits
sections.body: Quota and speed are configured on the recipient host. Autoselect does not debit pool members or inherit their speed limits. Multiple autoselects for one recipient share its allowance. Without recipient limits or enabled recipient tag limits, autoselect has no host-level ceiling. The account quota still applies. Xray JSON uses separate credentials for direct and autoselect connections. Direct access debits the member; autoselect debits only its recipient, with the recipient multiplier and enabled tag limits. User and device ceilings remain shared when switching members. Different recipients have independent limits. Access permissions, device bans, account status and destination restrictions still apply. Separate route accounting requires Node/Core with remnacust-routed-device-speed-v1; older components refuse routed policies. Update Node/Core before enabling it and refresh the subscription in the app. Old credentials retain their previous accounting; recorded history is not reassigned. If one host’s DENY overlaps a broader ALLOW_ONLY entry on the other, the overlapping allow entry is removed entirely.

sections.title: History and recovery
sections.body: Xray JSON, Singbox, Mihomo, Clash and Stash retain the last 30 saved versions. The database upgrade preserves existing code as the first version. History shows dates and a comparison with the current draft. Open in editor restores all code, including autoselect, balancers and assignments. Replacing an unsaved draft requires confirmation. Saving creates a new version, so a restore can itself be undone. An unsuccessful save changes neither code nor history.

sections.title: Autoselect in every editable format
sections.body: Autoselect is available for Xray JSON, sing-box, Mihomo, Clash and Stash. sing-box uses urltest/selector; YAML clients use url-test/select/fallback/load-balance. Groups can filter UUIDs, tags or regex with all/random/group and source visibility. Access is checked before selection; an empty explicit pool never becomes DIRECT. Manual members remain intact. Group name and default route are separate controls. All tabs share a draft; an unsaved Xray test pool can be removed with its dependent balancer. Forms show Save and Discard draft; code tools appear only in Editing.

sections.title: Geofiles library
sections.body: Ready-made datasets include published V2Fly and MetaCubeX GeoIP/GeoSite. Import uses the same HTTPS and content checks and never enables rules automatically. Use Click to upload for a local file. In Geofiles, upload from your computer or import a direct HTTPS URL, with a name and content format. Select a library item, attach it, select DAT categories and explicitly choose DIRECT, REJECT or a group. Multiple files and reuse across templates are supported. DAT becomes native rules on the server; sing-box JSON/SRS and Mihomo YAML/text use remote rule_set/rule-providers. Clash/Stash support YAML payload. Existing settings remain intact. Save the template and refresh the subscription to apply. File URLs are public: never upload secrets. Up to 32 files of 64 MiB, text up to 8 MiB; local addresses, archives and unrelated content are rejected. Preserve backups/geofiles when migrating: database-only backups exclude binary files. Historical versions may require reattachment after a file is deleted.

sections.title: Priority and backup servers
sections.body: Priority: first available selects the first working server. For an exact order, choose Hosts and All selected hosts, then reorder them with the arrows. Multiple pool prefixes can also be reordered in the balancer. Tags and regex follow the main host list; random modes select a subset first. Failover and return to the primary follow health checks and affect new connections; existing connections are not migrated. Xray JSON is rendered as standard single-candidate leastPing balancers with a Loopback chain. Connections are blocked before the first successful probe and when every server is unavailable. An explicit fallbackTag is used last. Selecting priority in the GUI removes the generated fallback to the same pool and preserves custom fallbacks. Probe settings are preserved. Limits: 128 candidates per balancer and 256 per configuration. Routing scripts and conflicting broad selectors of other balancers are incompatible. Mihomo/Clash/Stash use native fallback in proxies order: explicit code members precede pool members. sing-box has no automatic strict priority mode in its configuration; selector is manual and URLTest uses latency. A full JSON/YAML subscription is required.

sections.title: When to add the recipient host as proxy
sections.body: Also add the recipient host as proxy maps to remnawave.addVirtualHostAsOutbound. When enabled, the generator additionally builds a separate outbound tagged proxy from the recipient host’s address, port, transport and security settings. Autoselect does not require this switch; it does not enable TLS automatically. Leave it off for an Automatic placeholder representing a balancer. Real injectHosts pool members and the balancer remain in the configuration. Enable it only for a real additional connection supported by the client. A core may reject public VLESS without TLS/REALITY or VLESS encryption; Happ iOS proxy-based checks can report failed to build outbound config with tag proxy / vless without TLS. A successful ordinary test or another device does not validate this extra outbound. Disable the switch for a placeholder, or correct transport and security for a real host. Save the template and update the subscription in the app. The switch does not reconfigure servers or install certificates.

sections.title: Temporary delivery errors
sections.body: A failed user, device or host query does not mean the subscription was deleted. Configuration delivery returns a temporary error asking the client to retry after 30 seconds; a genuinely missing user still returns 404. A failed host query is not reported as a successful empty subscription. If there truly are no available hosts, extra template and quota queries are skipped. For repeated failures, check the log and database connectivity; do not replace a user’s keys to solve a network error.

sections.title: Output size and generation errors
sections.body: A generated subscription is limited to 16 MiB. Sing-box, Mihomo, Stash and Clash group expansion is also bounded during generation with room for escaping and formatting; excessive fanout may be rejected before reaching the exact limit. Reduce the number of groups or their servers. Generation failures return HTTP 503 rather than an empty successful subscription. When the cache is unavailable, templates are read from the database.

sections.title: Saving with warnings
sections.body: Save remains available for invalid JSON/YAML, empty host selections and incomplete geofile actions. Text with errors is saved on the server as a draft and included in history; reopening restores the same text. Subscriptions keep the last working configuration. Fix the warnings and save again: valid content replaces the working version and clears the draft. Network and database failures are not reported as successful saves.

sections.title: Host selection and balancing in one card
sections.body: Host sources and their strategy share one block. Pools using a shared balancer are grouped together; manual balancers remain visible. Deleting the block removes its sources, balancers and linked rules while retaining independent groups and manual outbounds. leastLoad.expected is the selected node count; tolerance is the allowed failed probe fraction from 0 to 1: 0.01 means 1%, and 2 does not mean two nodes. Xray clamps finite numeric values outside the range to 0–1; such templates apply with a warning while retaining the original number. New pools start with enabled hosts supported by the format, selected by UUID. With no eligible hosts, the setup remains a draft until sources are selected.

sections.title: When the app downloads geofiles
