sections.body: The panel measures each profile including list expansion and client formatting. Small datasets are inline rules; Happ/INCY download large datasets as DAT. A JSON subscription is required: enable “Serve JSON at the base subscription path” or use /json. Save the template and refresh the subscription.

sections.title: Automatic geofile delivery and size
sections.body: There is no manual delivery switch. All selected geofiles are first converted to inline rules. INCY receives long comma-free lists in lossless Xray StringList form. Each final profile is measured after four-space formatting against a geofile inline threshold of 90,000 bytes or 20,000 conditions; the full profile retains a conservative 900,000-byte panel budget with room for client patches; this is not a documented exact INCY limit. Host profiles are not added together for this comparison. A separate 16 MiB full-response transport limit remains. If a profile is too large, supported Happ/INCY receive bundled DAT with isolated category names. Inline compilation limits can also trigger downloads. Other Xray apps receive inline rules; an unsupported oversized configuration returns an error instead of losing rules. Small sing-box/Mihomo/Clash/Stash datasets are inline and large ones remote; binary SRS is always remote. Legacy Clash also downloads native providers for compatibility. DIRECT, REJECT, groups and routing order are preserved. Manual routing/geodata are not overwritten: incompatible oversized output fails explicitly. Profile names use the subscription profile-title, including squad overrides, or the subscription domain as fallback; a stable short suffix isolates identical names. Legacy downloadToClient is accepted but no longer chooses delivery. Client intervals apply only to remote delivery; server refresh has a separate schedule.

sections.title: Startup and concurrent requests
sections.body: After panel startup, different geofile builds wait in a bounded queue: two active tasks and up to 32 accepted tasks per operation. Identical requests share one build. The DAT cache retains at most 16 bundles and 32 MiB. The subscription page waits up to 30 seconds for the panel and cancels the request when the client disconnects; access failures are not cached. DAT downloads use a separate eight-connection pool. Each page process accepts up to 16 downloads including waiting requests, so slow files do not occupy page and configuration request connections. Overload returns 503 with Retry-After: 2; retry later.

sections.title: Removing a geofile from a template
sections.body: Save the template and refresh the subscription in the app. The profile keeps its name; the URL and all rule lists for the removed GeoIP or GeoSite kind are explicitly empty. If one of several files of the same kind is removed, the combined DAT contains only the remaining sources. Other app profiles and the shared file library are preserved.

sections.title: GeoIP for domain destinations
sections.body: When geofiles generate GeoIP rules, the final Xray JSON uses IPOnDemand: DNS resolution occurs when an IP rule is reached. DIRECT, REJECT and GeoIP balancers can then match before the TCP/UDP catch-all. Inline rules and downloaded DAT use the same behavior. Earlier manual rules retain priority and the source template is not overwritten. Domain-only GeoSite and other client formats keep their DNS strategy. If resolution fails, subsequent routing rules apply.

sections.title: Automatic geofile delivery and size
sections.body: There is no manual delivery switch. All selected geofiles are first converted to inline rules. INCY receives long comma-free lists in lossless Xray StringList form. Each final profile is measured after four-space formatting against a geofile inline threshold of 90,000 bytes or 20,000 conditions; the full profile retains a conservative 900,000-byte panel budget with room for client patches; this is not a documented exact INCY limit. Host profiles are not added together for this comparison. A separate 16 MiB full-response transport limit remains. If a profile is too large, supported Happ/INCY receive bundled DAT with isolated category names. Inline compilation limits can also trigger downloads. Other Xray apps receive inline rules; an unsupported oversized configuration returns an error instead of losing rules. Small sing-box/Mihomo/Clash/Stash datasets are inline and large ones remote; binary SRS is always remote. Legacy Clash also downloads native providers for compatibility. DIRECT, REJECT, groups and routing order are preserved. Manual routing/geodata are not overwritten: incompatible oversized output fails explicitly. Profile names use the subscription profile-title, including squad overrides, or the subscription domain as fallback; a stable short suffix isolates identical names. Legacy downloadToClient is accepted but no longer chooses delivery. Client intervals apply only to remote delivery; server refresh has a separate schedule. Size accounting includes Xray StringList expansion back into arrays: a small HTTP response can still produce a large client configuration. The 900,000-byte budget applies separately to each Happ/INCY profile. Geofile links use the HTTPS authority of the current subscription request, including CDN. The CDN and reverse proxy must preserve the original Host; arbitrary Forwarded/X-Forwarded-Host are not trusted. A subscription page relays its authority using its current scoped API token; update both components. Only links in that response change, not the configured panel server, signatures or DAT/.sha256 paths. Do not publicly cache subscriptions or geofiles on the CDN.

sections.title: Server auto downloads and update safety
sections.body: Select a library file and configure its HTTPS source, automatic updates and server interval from 15 minutes to 30 days. Settings save immediately for every template using that file. URL imports retain their source; PC uploads need a source URL. Auto updates default to off. The scheduler checks once a minute; a persisted lease prevents concurrent duplicate downloads. Source failure, panel restart and manual retries do not reset the interval. Addresses, redirects, size, format and categories used by active templates are validated. Errors retain the last working copy; status and next check are shown in the library. Original hashed URLs remain immutable; Updatable links and signed URLs return the active version without immutable caching. Server and client schedules are separate, so changes need not reach clients immediately.

sections.title: Shared catalog and pool members
sections.body: Ready-made datasets is one library for every template: PC uploads, URL imports and published sources. Import selects the entry without changing the template. Attach the file, choose categories and action, then save. Incompatible formats remain visible. Library deletion applies everywhere; detach files used by saved templates and save first. An unsaved attachment in the current editor is removed with the file. Pool members select connections; recipients of the entire template are separate optional settings below the code editor. The pool count excludes disabled hosts, duplicates and XRAY_JSON exclusions; user access and random selection can reduce the result. With legacy host naming, target the balancer rather than an unused prefix.

sections.title: Checking delivery in Happ and INCY
sections.body: No download animation is expected for a small subscription: its rules are already in JSON. Large profiles require full JSON and client routing support. Use /json or enable JSON at the base subscription path. Save the template actually assigned to the subscription, then refresh it. Routing profiles use the subscription title; a previously imported Remnacust name may remain as a separate entry that can be removed in the app. Check device preview and app logs to confirm delivery. Reconnect yourself if needed; the server never starts the tunnel.

sections.title: Refresh and file integrity
sections.body: The subscription page streams DAT separately from JSON: the 16 MiB JSON budget does not restrict DAT, which has a 64 MiB limit. Interrupted downloads are not successful. EOF or a missing category can indicate an incomplete or stale local file. Update both the panel and a separately installed subscription page, then refresh the subscription in the app. Compare DAT with its .sha256. Concurrent requests for the same bundle share one build; distinct work remains resource bounded. Bulk host updates commit to the database before the API response; node policy synchronization runs separately. Host editors fetch fresh data on open and save only changed fields to avoid restoring stale values after bulk updates. Some bulk user operations run in background queues; panel operations are not all deferred.

sections.title: Editing library files
sections.body:
Open Geofiles, choose a file in the shared library and select Edit file. The same action appears on an attached file. A preset requires a new name: saving creates an independent copy and replaces the source only in the current template draft. Save the template to apply that replacement. Other templates retain the original. Editing an ordinary uploaded file saves immediately and affects every template using it.

For DAT, select a category and browse or search paginated records. Edit domains, IPs and domain record types, remove records or add new ones. Attributes and other categories are preserved. Save or discard edits before changing categories. Text JSON/YAML sets can be edited in full up to 8 MiB; SRS and larger text files require a same-format replacement up to 64 MiB.

Manual editing disables automatic source refresh to preserve the changes. Concurrent administrator edits or refreshes cause a conflict rather than overwriting a newer revision: close and reopen the editor. A category used by a saved template cannot be removed without reconfiguring that template.

sections.title: Additional addresses and routes
sections.body:
Autoselect and geofiles share the Additional addresses section. Import accepts an Xray JSON rule, an array or comma-separated fragments, including a final comma. Choose one action for every address or retain the routes from the rules. Import creates separate rules in the current template; unsupported conditions reject the whole block rather than being silently dropped. Enter one domain, IP or CIDR per line and choose DIRECT, REJECT or an existing VPN/autoselect route. example.com includes subdomains; full:example.com is an exact match. keyword: and regexp: are also available. Domain and IP matches become independent rules rather than requiring both. Rules precede geofiles and the catch-all, making them useful exceptions.

These are rules in the current template: save it and refresh the app subscription. They do not change the shared library file. A block accepts at most 20,000 addresses and 2 MiB of text; upload larger lists as files. Complex manual rules with extra conditions remain in the code editor. For VPN, choose an existing working outbound or group: DIRECT or REJECT does not create a VPN server.

sections.title: Subscription refresh and personal links
sections.body: If a client still shows an old error after a panel release, verify that the subscription itself refreshed: when HTTPS on its old domain fails, the app keeps its saved configuration. Retain the old domain and certificate while migrating links; changing the panel address does not migrate installed subscriptions. Update a separately installed subscription page together with the panel. Personal /device/ links are bound to the subscription and HWID; the panel checks their signature, device block and user access on every request. Keep these links private. INCY receives long inline lists in lossless Xray string form; the size budget includes JSON formatting. Delivery is chosen automatically using each profile’s size.

sections.title: Selection and geofile editor workflow
sections.body: Each selection has one expandable card containing its servers, strategy and subscription host assignments. Assignments belong to a specific balancer name; renaming preserves the link. A legacy assignment with one possible selection appears inside it; ambiguous assignments require an explicit target. Opening the page does not rewrite code. Tabs scroll with the page; saving stays at the bottom. For geofiles, choose the library, computer or URL. Uploads immediately store the file in the shared library; a compatible file attaches to the current draft in one action. Set categories, action and the client interval in its card, then save the template; delivery is selected automatically. Detaching a file does not delete it from the library. Shared file settings and server refresh are in the expandable library section.

sections.title: INCY geofile checks
sections.body: INCY receives stable DAT URLs without query parameters. The signed file selection is in the path, so appending .sha256 to the complete URL returns the checksum for the same bundle. Unchanged files can be checked without downloading them again. Happ/INCY profile LastUpdated stays stable across unchanged subscription requests; a profile, file or delivery-mode change advances it. State is device-scoped and survives panel restarts. routing-geo-update-interval uses hours. Update a separately deployed subscription page together with the panel. Automatic inline delivery sends empty geofile URLs and disables periodic checks; the JSON keeps the rules. Previously issued URLs remain supported. Scheduling and network-error retries depend on the client version; the server does not start the tunnel. Official protocol: https://docs.incy.cc/routing/

sections.title: Pool membership after switching
sections.body: Switching grouped selection to connection-time selection merges UUID and tag groups into values. Regex and recipient-tag selectors retain their UUID boundary in groups: the original filter and user access both apply. Edit these lists in the GUI or code; unrelated hosts are excluded. Switching a manual client group to automatic selection sets its probe URL and interval.

sections.title: Selection at connection time
sections.body: Source pools and recipients are separate settings. Each remnawave.assignments entry binds a specific balancerTag to recipient hosts or tags. A direct host assignment takes precedence over a tag assignment. An explicit template in the host card remains highest priority; that template uses the balancer assigned to this recipient. DIRECT, REJECT and domain restrictions are preserved. all delivers every authorized source; the client strategy chooses a server for each new connection. random/group reduce membership when subscriptions refresh. Membership changes arrive on subscription refresh. A separate TCP entry for server changes is no longer created.

sections.title: Geofile thresholds and categories
sections.body: Inline rules are limited to 20,000 conditions per profile. For Happ/INCY the panel also reserves a 90,000-byte budget including client formatting and StringList expansion; this is the panel switching threshold, not a published application limit. Exceeding either threshold triggers a fresh render using DAT containing only selected categories. GeoSite and GeoIP are separate downloads; rule actions and order remain intact. Host profiles are never summed. Plain DIRECT/REJECT actions are not duplicated as direct/block; existing plain outbounds are reused without replacing custom outbound settings. Links are signed and earlier links remain supported. Preserve the entire backups/geofiles directory, including category selections, when migrating. Subscription and DAT URLs do not require a running VPN and use the public domain or configured CDN; HTTP 502, DNS and certificate failures require checking the external proxy and running subscription page. Download failure never becomes an empty successful dataset.

sections.title: Substitution context
sections.body: Variables are resolved when a subscription response is built for a particular user. Use supported names exactly: case and suffix matter. System values, dates, usage and quota describe response generation time, not continuously updating fields inside an already imported client file.

sections.title: Host and tag traffic
sections.body: {{TRAFFICLOCATIONUSEDGB}}, {{TRAFFICLOCATIONUSEDMB}} and corresponding LIMIT/LEFT variants return numeric values without units. Add GB/MB yourself if desired. Without TEG the context is the current host. TEG variants use tag context and fall back to the host when no tag is assigned. RESETAT describes reset time rather than bytes. The exact supported variable catalog is listed below.

sections.title: Example
sections.body: `DE · {{TRAFFICLOCATIONLEFTGBTEG}} GB` displays remaining tag-context quota. `{{TRAFFICLOCATIONUSEDMB}} MB` displays host usage. Subscription quota and location quota are distinct; choose the variable matching the desired counter.

sections.title: Delivery and headers
sections.body: Settings control response headers, subscription name/description, update interval, support links and default templates. Headers are delivered with a request and their presentation depends on the client. Custom remarks provide understandable entries for account states. External squads may override global delivery.

sections.title: HWID and actions
sections.body: Global HWID rules and fallback values live here; user-specific settings remain on the account. Delivered actions/buttons require compatible clients and do not replace administrator authorization. Test responses for active, disabled, expired and quota-limited accounts.

sections.title: Remark order
sections.body:
Open Subscription settings → the remarks card. Use the up and down arrows to move notification reasons, save the settings, then refresh the subscription in the client. The default order is Subscription expired, Subscription disabled, Subscription frozen, New devices denied, and Device blocked (HWID). Only messages for applicable reasons are shown. Each reason’s text is edited separately in this card.

When combining subscription status and HWID is enabled, an expired or disabled subscription together with a blocked device produces both message groups in the chosen order. For example, expiry appears before the device block by default; moving HWID above expiry reverses them. With combining disabled, the subscription status message takes priority; an active subscription shows the device block message.

New devices denied is handled separately. If registration is denied for a new device and its subscription is also expired or disabled, the reason placed higher in the list is shown. Moving registration denial above expiry therefore shows the registration message. These two reasons are not combined. An already registered, allowed device keeps access when the other access conditions are met.

Traffic quota exhaustion, the maximum device count and missing HWID support have separate messages outside this list. Reordering changes subscription messages; restrictions and access checks still apply. Presentation depends on the client.

sections.title: First start of a mixed node fleet
sections.body: Before preparing policy and credentials, the panel discovers capabilities of the node and peers sharing its inbounds. Discovery runs outside SQL transactions with bounded concurrency and time. Policy and configuration use the same compatibility snapshot. An unavailable node delays only affected inbounds; independent healthy nodes continue starting. Unknown compatibility keeps the previous configuration and schedules a retry. A network failure never classifies a node as native Remnawave or removes restrictions.

sections.title: Access lifetime and devices: UTC
sections.body: Access expiry and selected device timestamps use UTC independently of the PostgreSQL timezone. The update migrates access functions without changing stored dates, frozen lifetime or quotas. If a device is blocked or registered again after the list is opened, a stale bulk deletion preserves it.

sections.title: Subscription performance and compatibility
sections.body: Panel 1.1.7.95 checks issued identities and bulk configuration users using SQL sets while preserving expiry, status, squads, HWID blocks and key rotation. Node preflight precedes expensive configuration compilation; limit pauses are read in one query per node. Updates coalesce, at most three nodes synchronize per process, and a busy advisory lock is retried outside the transaction. A confirmed native Remnawave node receives a baseline configuration: new host restrictions, destination rules and inactive-user exceptions are disabled on its inbounds. A custom node sharing such an inbound uses the same compatible baseline credentials; isolated compatible inbounds retain extensions. Older custom cores without autoselect recipient accounting use ordinary pool-server credentials and limits. Upgrade Node/Core and refresh the client subscription for separate recipient accounting. The panel displays compatibility mode. An unknown node or network failure alone never disables restrictions. Existing quota reserves and financial fences are not erased by a downgrade. Older subscription-page APIs remain compatible, and pages hiding connection keys skip unused link generation. This mode needs no new .env variables; the UTC access-expiry migration is described separately.

sections.title: Technical update log
sections.body: Download journal in the panel update dialog and subscription page operations downloads real technical output rather than a status JSON. Only a panel administrator can download it for the current job ID; API tokens cannot. Passwords and tokens are removed from the downloaded copy. Large files return the last 1 MiB with a truncation notice; the complete private file remains on the server until the next operation for that component. If the panel is temporarily unreachable, retry after reconnection or open the displayed server path. Requires panel 1.1.7.91 and installer service 1.2.129. remnacust-panel-update.service starts the local API at boot and only starts updates on an administrator request.

sections.title: Inactive access and freezing
sections.body: Hosts enabled for inactive subscription access are available for EXPIRED, DISABLED, FROZEN and LIMITED, and for an ACTIVE account whose time has expired. The additional option hides them while the subscription is active. Squad permissions, device blocks and host-specific limits still apply. Configure the FROZEN block and its position in remark order under custom remarks. {{FREE_HOST}} inserts permitted hosts at that line; it cannot bypass an HWID block or grant access. Add that host’s inbound to the user’s internal squad. For a shared inbound, restrict other hosts through their squad access settings to avoid granting extra connections. Device preview warns when only notifications remain after resolving credentials. External squads may override wording and order. Older settings gain default frozen wording without replacing saved messages. Inactive JSON uses standalone connections without shared or assigned templates, balancers or geofiles; host restrictions still apply. Domains, IPs and networks become separate rules. HWID denial shows the saved device-limit or unsupported-device warning instead of only subscription status. Happ and INCY on the same PC use different HWIDs and occupy separate device slots.

sections.title: Multiple subscription links
sections.body: The user card shows the regular URL and up to three CDNs of the selected primary domain. Each link has copy and QR actions; the preferred domain is marked. Expiration, freezing, devices and quotas remain shared. API tokens may grant regular links only, CDN links only or all links; routes and filters are described in the API reference. Catalog access alone never grants access to subscription keys. A fourth CDN cannot be created or moved into a full family. Remove existing excess records manually.

sections.title: CDN: configure once
sections.body: Copy the individual neutral request header name and UUID value from Set up CDN. Add an origin request header in VK or Yandex. The name stays stable across upgrades; replace only the old common header name when migrating. Use the main subscription site for the HTTPS origin, Host and SNI. Disable forced caching of personalized responses. Existing client URLs need no replacement; files, checksums and device URLs retain the CDN. The ID does not bypass keys, status, freezing, expiry or HWID. The /cdn/<ID> path remains a fallback for CDNs without request headers. No new .env variables are needed. The name is generated with the private installation key and cannot be computed from the public ID alone. If APP_SECRET is separately rotated, copy the new header name to the CDN.

sections.title: Subscription domain and .env
sections.body: The primary domain and SUB_PUBLIC_DOMAIN are synchronized both ways through the local installer service. The API checks .env at startup, when opening the list and every 30 seconds. Changing the primary address in the panel updates .env and the registered Compose without a restart. A hostname, HTTPS URL and safe path are supported. CDN domains remain in the registry. The domain list API requires panel 1.1.7.78 or later to avoid the authentication dependency error. Installer 1.2.113 or later is required; a missing service shows an unavailable status rather than a false confirmation. Concurrent file changes prevent overwrites. Configure DNS and certificates separately.

sections.title: Subscription refresh and HWID
sections.body:
Subscription delivery checks the user, device, registration policy and device limit in the database without waiting for nodes. Personal keys are delivered separately through persistent jobs with retries. If a node is unavailable, the subscription is still returned; a new connection on that node becomes usable after its key arrives. Known devices do not wait for the lock used to register new devices. Refreshing a known device does not resend keys to every node, but rechecks authorization: HWID blocks and registration restrictions remain enforced.

A website visit or curl request without device headers does not exercise the same path as Happ or INCY. Compare the same URL with the application User-Agent and HWID when diagnosing failures. Do not publish subscription URLs or HWIDs in public logs.

sections.title: Pages on this server
sections.body: The Subscription pages tab manages registered instances on the panel server: start, stop, restart and independent update. Installer 1.2.100 and its local control service are required. CLI commands: install-subscription-page, upgrade-subscription-page --page-id ID, and manage-subscription-page; the list shows IDs. A local panel uses a separate restricted token and Docker network. A remote panel requires HTTPS and a subscription-page API token. Page ports bind to loopback; use a separate Caddy on free HTTPS ports or your existing proxy. Updates preserve settings and stopped state; failed readiness rolls Compose back. Private operation logs: /opt/remnacust/logs/page-<id>.log. Browser requests cannot supply arbitrary commands, paths or images.

sections.title: Existing Remnawave pages
sections.body: Local discovery also includes legacy Remnawave Compose pages connected to this exact panel. It checks the official image, connection to the panel and its network, Compose identity and safe files. Listing does not register or change the deployment. Legacy pages support start, stop and restart; their image, token and settings are preserved. Migrate explicitly with the installer before upgrading. Remote pages, non-Compose deployments, connections to another panel and unsafe paths are not accepted for management. Registered pages retain their existing controls.

sections.title: Page connection to the panel
sections.body: During page installation or migration, choose the local panel or another panel’s HTTPS address and an API token with subscription-page permissions. Option 9 in the installer’s page management changes the panel and token. Enter the token privately or use a private file with mode 0600. Connectivity and permissions are checked first; failed application restores the previous settings. Only the selected page changes, and stopped pages remain stopped. An existing Remnacust image is not offered for migration again.

sections.title: Conditions and order
sections.body: Rules choose a subscription response from request conditions, such as the app name in the User-Agent header. Add a rule, set its conditions and response format or template, then enable it. Rule order affects response selection. The app list is built from positive conditions in enabled rules; an app missing from that list is not necessarily blocked.

sections.title: Responses and testing
sections.body: Open the matching test and supply the same headers as the client. Check the selected rule and result: a configuration, rejection, HTTP 404/451 or closed connection. If the result is wrong, review rule order and condition operators, then test again. After saving, refresh the subscription in the app itself; a browser may receive a different response.

sections.title: Page configurations
sections.body: A configuration defines subscription page presentation and content, including text, applications, instructions and supported options. Create variants and assign them using the supported user/external-squad settings. It is neither a server profile nor an independent traffic limit.

sections.title: Delivery
sections.body: After saving, open a test user’s subscription page. Check the chosen variant, language, application links and mobile layout. The subscription link gives access to the user’s data; share it only with its owner.

sections.title: Displayed scopes
sections.body: Select an individual host or a tag grouping hosts under a shared quota. The page shows scopes with a quota, speed restriction or block. Scopes without restrictions or a block are hidden.

sections.title: Columns
sections.body: Compare usage, effective quota, remaining traffic, one-time bonus and access status in the table. A 100 GiB base quota plus a 20 GiB bonus provides 120 GiB; after 80 GiB of accounted usage, 40 GiB remains. Unlimited removes the personal quota in the selected scope, but usage is still counted. It does not override a traffic pause, subscription expiration or other user restrictions.

sections.title: Search and state
sections.body: Search by username, identifier, email or Telegram ID. Use status, availability and squad filters, sorting and page size. “Traffic blocked: N of M recipients” refers to the selected recipient mode, not only visible rows.

sections.title: When the panel is unavailable
sections.body: Compatible nodes use quota reserves allocated in advance. While the panel is unavailable, connections can use the remaining local reserve; a new reserve requires connectivity. Exhausting it does not grant unlimited access. A reset applies immediately to reachable nodes; others receive it when reconnecting. While an unreachable node spends its old reserve, total usage can temporarily exceed the new quota. Speed caps and other local rules remain active.

sections.title: Add traffic and reset usage
sections.body: Adding traffic grants a one-time addition to an existing positive quota for the selected host or tag. Resetting restarts the current period’s usage counter while retaining historical statistics. It does not revoke a personal unlimited allowance.

sections.title: Blocking and unblocking
sections.body: Blocking pauses traffic for the selected host or tag and recipients. Unblocking removes that pause. It does not extend a subscription, enable a disabled user or add traffic. A block affecting the entire scope and a personal user block apply together.

sections.title: Selecting recipients
sections.body: For one user, select only their row. A bulk action can target selected users, all current recipients with access or members of a chosen squad. Search and pagination do not restrict “All” or “Squad” mode. Check the mode and recipient count before confirming. If the result is unclear, refresh the table before granting more traffic.

sections.title: Grant and revoke
sections.body: Grant unlimited saves a personal exemption for the selected host/tag. It persists until explicitly revoked, across restarts and period changes. Scope settings remain unchanged. Revoke unlimited restores the current base quota with existing bonus allowance. To grant it to one person, select only that user.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: Unlimited exempts only that scope’s quota. Pauses, bandwidth caps, expiry, status, HWID and other scopes still apply; usage remains recorded. Bulk grants target current recipients; future users and future squad members do not inherit them.

sections.title: Distinct restrictions
sections.body: A user quota is data volume. Host per-user bandwidth caps one user, while shared bandwidth is a common cap. The multiplier changes charged volume rather than connection speed. Applicable restrictions operate together; unlimited status in one quota does not disable the others.

sections.title: Period reset
sections.body: Host/tag reset intervals use days or months; 0 means no automatic reset. The quota window uses the saved configuration anchor date. Changing a multiplier recalculates current scope accounting under policy rules without changing ordinary subscription usage. Inspect current allowance, bonus and usage before changing a period.

sections.title: Device overview
sections.body: The inspector aggregates devices, applications and platforms, with distributions and user lists. It describes registered data; incompatible clients may supply no HWID. Search and filters locate entries; account-specific management is available in the user card.

sections.title: Interpretation
sections.body: OS and application names come from client headers and are not guaranteed hardware identity. Missing device records do not prove there are no connections. Use the dedicated HWID blocking action and verify ownership.

sections.title: What is recorded
sections.body: History shows subscription fetches, with user, time, address, client headers and outcome where recorded. These are configuration requests, not all internet traffic through the proxy. The user card opens account history; the global inspector helps compare requests and diagnose delivery.

sections.title: Empty history
sections.body: Check whether the client fetched its subscription and whether SRH recording or retention is disabled. Client caching may reduce requests. A fetch record alone does not confirm successful proxy connection after import.

sections.title: Collecting state
sections.body: Choose a user or node and collect connections. Some operations create a job whose result is fetched afterward; the list is not an instantaneous snapshot of the entire infrastructure. Search supports username, ID, IP and node. The Recording tab accepts 1–10080 minutes and a 10–300 second interval. Recording continues on the server when the tab closes. JSON contains users, current subscription links, IPs, nodes and observation times; store it privately. Up to 20 recordings are retained for 3 days after completion. Recording stops with a warning at 20,000 user/node/IP combinations. Offline nodes and failed polls are reported separately. Short connections between polls may be missed. The available node count is shown before starting. The node list is reloaded before every scan; no separate refresh button is needed. Loading errors, empty lists and disconnected nodes have separate explanations. Start scan also retries loading after an error or an empty list. IP observation does not require NET_ADMIN. Update the node and wait for the panel to apply its configuration to enable observation. Personal device and host sessions are grouped by owner. A failed poll is not a successful empty response; partial results show failed polls and unknown Xray identities.

sections.title: Dropping connections
sections.body: Drop connections closes current sessions for the selected target. It does not disable the account: an allowed client can reconnect. For persistent denial use account status, HWID blocking or the relevant quota scope pause. Collect another snapshot after dropping sessions.

sections.title: Node permissions
sections.body: Reading active-connection IPs through Xray does not require NET_ADMIN. Additional Linux features on the node use it. Node installation and updates ask about it separately when it cannot be confirmed in the running container. An already effective capability is kept without another prompt. For automation, use --net-admin or --no-net-admin; a cap_add entry in an old Compose file alone does not prove the capability is effective.

sections.title: Purpose
sections.body: The page displays HTTP request statistics collected by the server, helping identify busy routes and errors. These are panel metrics rather than node usage or a list of user browsing destinations. Review filters and time range before comparing results.

sections.title: Missing or old data
sections.body: Disabled collection or a server restart may leave no data or a short history. Refresh updates the display but cannot reconstruct statistics that were never collected.

sections.title: Policy and reports
sections.body: The feature requires the corresponding node mechanism/plugin and account settings. The user card switch sets policy; reports show recorded events. No reports do not prove there were no attempts if collection or the plugin is unavailable.

sections.title: Verification
sections.body: Check plugin assignment, synchronization and the report range. Torrent restrictions are separate from disabling the entire account or deleting HWID registrations.

sections.title: Access relationships
sections.body: Choose a user and host to inspect linked profiles, nodes, inbounds, outbounds and applicable rules. Filters highlight available, disabled, hidden or quota-limited hosts.

sections.title: Model limitations
sections.body: The diagram is built from panel configuration rather than tracing each packet. Actual behavior depends on DNS, core routing, destination availability and node health. Use logs and active sessions to investigate a real failure.

sections.title: Access and files
sections.body: A fresh panel installation asks for a backup password; Enter generates one automatically. The installer shows it when installation finishes and saves it in `backup-password.txt` in the panel directory, accessible only to root. Keep a copy away from the server. Administrators unlock this section with that password. Click “Create ZIP backup” and wait for the file to appear. The encrypted archive contains a database dump and requires its password to open. Download it to separate storage. Sending transfers the selected file to Telegram, deleting removes it from the server, and “Lock access” locks the section again. The database backup excludes the server’s .env, certificates and node files. There is no restore button in the panel; restoration is performed by the server administrator. The ZIP uses AES. After extraction, database.dump is still a compressed PostgreSQL custom dump, without additional encryption. It is not readable in a text editor. Convert to SQL without restoring a database: `pg_restore --file=database.sql database.dump`. Use PostgreSQL tools of the same major version as pg_dump or newer.

sections.title: Automatic creation
sections.body: Enable automatic backups, select a period from 1 to 168 hours and retention from 1 to 7 days, then save. Disabling automation stops new scheduled backups; older files continue to expire according to the retention setting.

sections.title: Telegram delivery
sections.body: For automatic delivery, enable it and enter the bot token and chat or group ID. Save the settings and check that a backup arrives. If creation or delivery fails, read the panel’s error message; server configuration is handled by the installation administrator.

sections.title: Sign-in methods
sections.body: Settings support password, configured OAuth2 providers and passkeys. Enable only configured methods; changing a login button does not configure the provider automatically. Passkeys require a compatible browser/device. Administrator sessions and API tokens serve different purposes.

sections.title: Terms and sign-out
sections.body: Until panel terms are accepted, navigation to other pages returns to Home. Sign-out ends the current administrator session; revoking an admin session does not disable every subscription user. Do not disable the only working sign-in method without another verified method.

sections.title: Creating and editing
sections.body: Create a separate token for each integration in settings. Specify a clear name, expiry and required permissions. Save after changing permissions. Deleting a token or reaching its expiry stops the integration’s access.

sections.title: Choosing permissions
sections.body: Grant access only to the required sections and actions. Read access retrieves data; write access permits the allowed changes. Access to all operations does not unlock administrative actions unavailable to API tokens. Granting unlimited traffic requires the corresponding permission. Exact methods and permissions are listed in the separate API reference.

sections.title: Token handling
sections.body: Share the token only with a trusted integration. If exposed, delete it and create a replacement. The token name helps identify which service uses the access. Access for individual customers is managed by the integration itself.

sections.title: Reading private settings through the API
sections.body: Node API responses exclude raw inbound settings and private keys. Use the profile API with the appropriate permission to read configuration. Updating a profile requires update permission and config-profiles:get; updating a template requires update permission and subscription-template:get because the response contains stored content. Matching :read, :* or * scopes also permit reading. Without read access, the request is rejected before changing data. Updating, enabling, disabling or extending users, resetting their traffic and revoking subscriptions also require users:by-id. Updating an external squad requires external-squads:get; reordering requires external-squads:list. Matching :read and :* grants also apply. Creating a user does not require reading existing keys. Administrator sessions keep their existing behavior.

sections.title: User-management bots and permanent access
sections.body: The Users preset permits creating, editing, freezing/resuming users, resetting traffic, reading subscription keys and links, and bulk user operations. It is a fixed list of 30 users-resource scopes; HWID management and squad/domain catalogs require separate selection. It excludes panel settings, servers, backups and token administration. In the user API, set status FROZEN to freeze and ACTIVE to resume. Required scopes: users:update or users:write, plus users:by-id or users:read; users:* covers both. Expired accounts freeze with zero remaining time. When creating a token select No expiration: expiresInDays: null stores expireAt: null and signs a JWT without exp with an explicit permanent marker. No fabricated distant date is used. Every request checks deletion and current scopes in the database. Editing names/permissions preserves token value and expiry; create a replacement and delete the old token to change lifetime. The minimum subscription-page preset contains only system:metadata, subscriptions:subpage-config, subscription-page-configs:get and subscription-page-configs:list. Add users:by-username separately only for enabled Marzban legacy-link compatibility.

sections.title: Interface preferences
sections.body: Choose the panel language and a comfortable appearance: light or dark theme, accent color, font, density and navigation style. These settings change the interface presentation.

sections.title: Reducing motion
sections.body: Enable “Reduce motion” if you prefer a calmer interface. The panel also respects the equivalent device setting.

sections.title: Updating from the panel
sections.body:
When a new version is available, the header version number uses the theme accent color. Click it to find Update below the support and GitHub buttons. For an older installation, run upgrade-panel with the new installer once to configure the update service.

Starting an update blocks all open panel sessions. The installer checks the release, backs up the database and updates the applications while preserving keys, volumes and Compose settings. Nodes and existing Nginx/Caddy are not updated. Closing the browser does not stop the operation. After the applications restart, the page reloads. If the update fails, read the message and check panel-update-<identifier>.log in the installer logs directory before retrying.

The update dialog shows the current stage out of eight, stage completion percentage, elapsed time and stages after the current one. The journal contains the 24 most recent step events and can be downloaded as JSON; full technical output remains in a private server file. Remaining time is estimated from a previous successful update, or remaining stages are shown when no history exists. During an API restart the dialog retains the last confirmed progress until reconnection; expected PANEL_UPDATING errors do not create notifications.

Release checks (--check-release and checking for a new version in the panel) do not run APT, install packages or update applications. An SSH requirement for system package configuration must not stop a release check.

During a background panel update, OS maintenance is deferred to a separate SSH session and recorded in progress and the private log; the available component update continues. This does not mean OS packages have been updated. Perform OS maintenance separately in an SSH terminal: the interactive CLI retains apt-get update and upgrade -y, while the operator answers actual dpkg/debconf questions. --yes does not choose package configuration answers. The installer never reboots the server automatically. Deferring OS maintenance does not turn a backup, migration or application update failure into success.

sections.title: Appearance reset
sections.body: Reset in theme settings restores the default theme, accent, font, interface density and motion setting. Changes apply immediately and are saved in this browser.

sections.title: Theme settings
sections.body: Open the palette in the header. Checkmarks identify the selected theme and accent, and the current accent name appears above the palette. Choose a font from the list; interface density and motion have switches below. Changes apply immediately and are saved in this browser; no separate Save button is needed. Reset restores the default theme, accent, font, density and motion.

sections.title: Panel events
sections.body: The server administrator configures general user, node and service notifications in the installation settings: enable delivery, set the bot token and choose chats for each event type. The panel has no separate form covering all these parameters. Automatic backup delivery is configured separately on the Backups page and can use a different bot.

sections.title: Checking delivery
sections.body: After changing settings, verify that notifications arrive. If messages are missing, check the token, recipient and the bot’s access to the chat. Report delivery failures to the administrator with the event time and panel message.

sections.title: Unable to save
sections.body: Read the panel message and check required fields. Sign in again if your session has expired. Contact the administrator if access is denied. If the error persists, record its text, time and the action you were taking for support.

sections.title: Connection does not work
sections.body:
1. Check user status and subscription expiry.
2. Check the overall quota, host or tag limits and device restrictions.
3. Ensure the internal squad permits the required inbound.
4. Check node health, profile, host and logs.
5. Refresh the subscription in the client and retry the connection.
If a bulk operation’s result is unclear, check recipient state before repeating it.

sections.title: Arguments and Base64
sections.body: Arguments follow a colon and use | separators: `{{NEXT_TRAFFIC_RESET_AT:format=DD.MM.YYYY HH:mm}}`, `{{STATUS:ACTIVE=Active|DISABLED=Disabled|EXPIRED=Expired|LIMITED=Limited}}`. RESET_STRATEGY accepts NO_RESET, DAY, WEEK, MONTH and MONTH_ROLLING labels. `rwEncodeBase64:` encodes the rendered string and adds `base64:`. An unknown variable remains literal text.

sections.title: Numbers, infinity and context
sections.body: LOCATION MB/GB variants use base 1024, up to three decimal places and no unit; unlimited LIMIT/LEFT returns ∞. Ordinary TRAFFIC_USED_MB/GB and TOTAL_TRAFFIC_MB/GB include units. Without a current host, LOCATION headers can return a deduplicated semicolon-separated name: value list. Multiple tags can also produce a TEG list. LOCATION RESETAT dates use UTC.

sections.title: Time values
sections.body: UNIX values are seconds, not milliseconds. Missing LAST_TRAFFIC_RESET_AT_UNIX/NEXT_TRAFFIC_RESET_AT_UNIX is 0; formatted variants are empty. DAYS_LEFT is clamped at zero. Ordinary TRAFFIC_LEFT for an unlimited subscription is 0 according to the counter rules, not ∞; it differs from LOCATION LEFT.

sections.title: Connections and unique users
sections.body: Online on nodes sums connections across nodes; one account connected to two nodes can appear twice. Online users counts unique accounts, so the cards may differ while the system is healthy. See the [Remnawave quick start](https://docs.rw/learn-en/quick-start/).

sections.title: Traffic comparison
sections.body: The Today card compares its current measurement period against a previous period; node reports update the values. Zero on a new panel does not by itself prove a fault. Check the measurement time, period and a real client connection.

sections.title: Password and session
sections.body: Administrators sign in on the login page. After changing authentication, verify a working sign-in in another session and recovery access. The official [quick start](https://docs.rw/learn-en/quick-start/) describes a Rescue CLI for lost passwords; check container names for your installation.

sections.title: Passkey
sections.body: A passkey is registered for an administrator device/browser and can be viewed or removed in Settings. Registration and login are separate operations; adding a key does not automatically disable another login method. WebAuthn requires the correct panel domain and HTTPS.

sections.title: OAuth2
sections.body: Configure the Client ID, Client Secret and redirect URI with the selected provider. For Generic OAuth2, set the authorization and token endpoints, panel domain and exact issuer from the provider’s OpenID Connect configuration. The issuer can include a path; its trailing / matters too. The panel compares it with the ID token’s iss and rejects a response from another issuer. When upgrading an existing configuration, fill in this field before signing in through Generic OAuth2 again. Keep a working login method until you have tested the new one in a separate session. Administrator OAuth2 login and API tokens are configured separately.

title: What happens when a subscription is opened

sections.title: One URL, different responses
sections.body: A user opens the subscription link in a browser or adds it to an app. A browser may receive an instruction page while an app receives a configuration in the selected format. The panel considers request headers and response rules. If the app receives no connections, find its request in request history and check the response format, user status and HWID.

sections.title: Generation pipeline
sections.body: A host defines a connection entry point and maps to one inbound. A template selects the configuration format, response rules choose delivery behavior, subscription settings add metadata, and an external squad can override templates and settings. Troubleshoot each stage separately.

sections.title: Format families
sections.body: Templates are separated by client family, including Mihomo, Xray JSON, sing-box and Base64 fallback. Select the template for the actual client; a server inbound does not guarantee that every client generator represents its transport. Check rendered JSON and generator support for new core features.

sections.title: External squads and response rules
sections.body: An external squad can override a template for a group. Response rules select how subscription output is generated from request conditions. After edits, inspect one user’s request history and the actual client output. The [official overview](https://docs.rw/learn-en/quick-start/) separates templates and delivery rules.

sections.title: Addresses and networks
sections.body: Choose “Support the project” in the documentation contents to open the addresses page directly. It is also available in the additional options menu. The page lists Gram on TON, Solana, TRC20 on TRON, Litecoin, Ethereum and Bitcoin addresses. Find the required network in the list and click Copy. Check the full address in your wallet before sending; the currency and network must match the selected network.

sections.title: How the page works
sections.body: Copy places the address on the clipboard. The panel does not connect a wallet, sign or send a transfer, charge funds or create a subscription. The Telegram link opens contact with the project author for questions and suggestions.
